name: Acode
use_label: Write and run code on an Android phone
one_liner: A code editor for Android with a built-in Linux terminal and instant preview.

text.why: When something needs fixing and you are not at a computer, the options are thin. Acode lets you edit HTML, CSS and JavaScript on an Android device and preview it in a browser immediately, and reaches server files through its built-in terminal and S/FTP and SSH connections.
text.take: The terminal is what separates it from other mobile editors: you can finish a loop on the phone instead of only typing into a file.
build: An Android app written in JavaScript: syntax support for many languages, a built-in JavaScript console, an Alpine-based terminal, S/FTP and SSH, community plugins and multi-language support. Available from Google Play, F-Droid and GitHub.

who.role: People fixing a site on the move, students working from a tablet, and anyone who has to touch a server without a laptop.

start.text: Install from Google Play or F-Droid and open a file.

caveat: The source is MIT, but the official site also sells a Pro tier. Android only — and long code on a small screen is still long code on a small screen.

license.scope_text: Use, change and redistribute, commercially too. Keep the notice.

numbers.star_delta_unit: GitHub stars gained in the window, GH Archive events summed to as_of
numbers.method: Star total = the value last checked on GitHub (stars_checked_at) + increases observed via GH Archive since. The 24h · 7d · 30d gains are GH Archive hourly events summed to the reference time (as_of). No score of ours.
